## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nandamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Nanda") is a sutta in the *Pārāyaṇavagga*, the fifth chapter of the *Suttanipāta*, comprising verses 1077–1083 [Hazra 1994; Norman 1997-2001]. In this dialogue, the student Nanda questions the Buddha about the nature of a sage (*muni*) and how one crosses beyond birth and old age [Wiltshire 1990]. The Buddha explains that one is not acknowledged as a *muni* merely on account of holding philosophical views or possessing knowledge, since purity does not originate from either of these [Hazra 1994]. Ascetics and brahmins who uphold opposing views and conduct themselves accordingly fail to cross over birth and aging, whereas those free of such grasping succeed [Hazra 1994]. Metrically, the verses are composed predominantly in Triṣṭubh, with certain pādas in Śloka metre [Norman 1997-2001].

The text was incorporated into the canonical commentary preserved in the *Cullaniddesa*, specifically *Nandamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 11) and *Pucchā* (Cnd 2). In computational analysis by DharmaNexus, extensive Pali-internal reuse is recorded with Cnd 11 (118 matching segments) and Cnd 2 (20 matching segments), as well as shared verses or phrasing with *Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchā* (Snp 5.4) and other *Niddesa* sections [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus identifies machine-aligned textual correspondences with the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) [DharmaNexus].
